parts.//import: The specifier other parts import this one as. A package subpath, so a consumer writes an ordinary import and TypeScript resolves it through this package's own `exports` -- no paths mapping, no generator, and `ui.Card({ wrong: 1 })` fails to compile. The builder marks it external and the site's import map points it at this artifact, exactly as it has always done for @flybyme/mesh-web.
parts.//why: Fourteen components and composites that nothing could render. A part is bundled with one specifier external and everything else inlined from its own clone, so no part outside this repository could import them -- which is why element('Label') threw on a page whose node_modules contained Label.
parts.description: The vocabulary: eleven components and three composites, themed from the thirteen tokens, with no DOM call anywhere in them.
The credential seam: holds the session, attaches the ticket, handles revocation. A site that has no accounts does not load it.
parts.//mesh: The three calls the Extension makes by path, declared so a site actually grants them. Without this a site could load auth and expose no way to sign in -- the api would 404 /api/identity/ticket and the page would report a network failure for a route that exists and was simply not granted.

parts.description: Who may act, and where. Organizations, their members, and the roles those members hold.

mesh.//contracts: The key is `contracts`, not `consumes`. `requirementsOf` flat-maps `mesh[].contracts` and reads nothing else, so this list declared no requirement at all and a site built from it would grant identity nothing -- the same empty-descriptor failure flowboard had.
